name: Ranitidine
executiveSummary: H2 antagonist. Adult IV 50 mg every 6–8 h (max 400 mg/day); pediatric IV 2–4 mg/kg/day. Note: withdrawn/restricted in many markets due to NDMA impurities — prefer PPI or available H2 blockers per local protocol.
indications:
## Indications (historical / if still locally authorized)

- Peptic ulcer, GERD, hypersecretion; stress-ulcer prophylaxis in critical care.

## Regulatory alert

- ANMAT/FDA/EMA withdrew or restricted ranitidine due to **NDMA**. Verify institutional availability and substitute omeprazole/pantoprazole/famotidine per local guidance.

> Use only if the product remains authorized and available at the center.

adulto.presentation: Ampoules 10 mg/mL (e.g. 50 mg/5 mL); tablets 150–300 mg (if available).
adulto.dose: IV: **50 mg every 6–8 h**; max **400 mg/day**. PO (if available): **150 mg every 12 h** or **300 mg at night** (ulcer/GERD per historical label).
adulto.administration: IV: dilute to 0.5–2.5 mg/mL in 0.9% NaCl or 5% dextrose; infuse 15–30 min (avoid rapid bolus — bradycardia).
adulto.notes: Adjust in renal failure. Caution in hepatic impairment.

pediatrico.dose: Children IV: **2–4 mg/kg/day** divided every 6–8 h. Preterm and term neonates < 2 weeks: load **1.5 mg/kg**, then **1.5 mg/kg/day** every 12 h. Adults: see adult section.
pediatrico.notes: Prefer current alternatives (PPI) unless institutional protocol still uses ranitidine.

neonatal.dose: Preterm / < 2 weeks: IV load **1.5 mg/kg**; maintenance **1.5 mg/kg/day** every 12 h. Adjust for renal function.
neonatal.notes: Check whether the center still stocks the drug; many NICUs migrated to PPI/famotidine.

stability:
## Stability / storage

- Dilution: usual stability up to 48 h at room temperature per card (verify residual label/lot).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Headache, dizziness, insomnia/agitation, rash, constipation/diarrhea, nausea. Bradycardia with rapid infusion. Rare: ↑ transaminases, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, bronchospasm.
